root_cause.text: Skipping inode reference acquisition in fuse_prepare_release() when the server does not implement open (due to commit e26ee4efbc79) allowed the inode to be evicted during inflight readahead requests, creating a deadlock where reclaim waiting on a locked folio (via truncate_inode_pages_range) blocks the readahead that itself is waiting on reclaim.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description and patch explicitly state: "fuse_prepare_release() now skips grabbing the reference on the inode, which makes it possible for an inode to be evicted from the dcache while there are inflight readahead requests. This causes a deadlock if the server triggers reclaim while servicing the readahead request and reclaim attempts to evict the inode...". The fix reallocates ff->release_args (and thus grabs the inode reference) even when the server does not implement open.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix handling of FUSE_RELEASE when the server does not implement 'open' by skipping the request and releasing locally, and correct the related comment.
intent_record.what: Changed comment in fuse_file_put from 'open' to 'opendir', and added an else-if branch that checks if args->opcode is FUSE_RELEASE and ff->fm->fc->no_open is set, then calls fuse_release_end directly instead of falling through to the sync path.
intent_record.how: The new branch prevents sending a FUSE_RELEASE request to a server that does not support the 'open' operation (no_open flag set). Instead, it completes the release locally by calling fuse_release_end without a request, which avoids unnecessary communication and potential errors.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix potential deadlock by always allocating release args for regular files, even when `fc->no_open` is set.
intent_record.what: Added a boolean variable `release` set to `!isdir || open` and changed the `fuse_file_alloc` call to pass `release` instead of `open`. Also added a comment explaining the need for this change.
intent_record.how: For regular files (`isdir == false`), `release` is now always `true`, ensuring `fuse_file_alloc` always allocates `release_args`. This prevents a deadlock scenario where reclaim could occur while servicing a readahead request, by allowing an inode reference to be held during `->release()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix a bug where `ff->args` was incorrectly freed for non-directory file opens, potentially causing use-after-free; now only free when opening a directory.
intent_record.what: Moved the lines `kfree(ff->args); ff->args = NULL;` from before the if-else block into the `if (isdir)` branch only, and added braces to the else branch.
intent_record.how: Previously, for non-directory files, the code would free the args and set the field to NULL. After the change, those operations only happen when isdir is true; for non-directories the args are left intact.

bic_trace_step.commit_msg:
fuse: allocate ff->release_args only if release is needed

This removed the need to pass isdir argument to fuse_put_file
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit e26ee4efbc79610b20e7abe9d96c87f33dacc1ff
Author: Amir Goldstein <amir73il@gmail.com>
Date:   Thu Feb 1 15:30:05 2024 +0200

    fuse: allocate ff->release_args only if release is needed
    
    This removed the need to pass isdir argument to fuse_put_file().
    
    Signed-off-by: Amir Goldstein <amir73il@gmail.com>
    Signed-off-by: Miklos Szeredi <mszeredi@redhat.com>

diff --git a/fs/fuse/file.c b/fs/fuse/file.c
index 1b403350a5d5..bdda420f5acf 100644
--- a/fs/fuse/file.c
+++ b/fs/f
bic_trace_step.reason: The commit moves the inode reference acquisition into fuse_prepare_release(), but only does igrab() when 'ra' (release_args) is non-NULL and sync is false. When the server does not implement open, 'ra' is NULL (because release_args is not allocated), so fuse_prepare_release() returns early at line 'if (!ra) return;' without taking an inode reference. Later, fuse_file_put() also does nothing when 'ra' is NULL (line 'if (!args) { /* Do nothing ... */ }'). This skips the required inode refcount increment, which can lead to inode eviction during inflight readahead requests and a deadlock. The vulnerability is present in this commit.

Author: Max Reitz <mreitz@redhat.com>

    fuse: split fuse_mount off of fuse_conn
    
    We want to allow submounts for the same fuse_conn, but with different
    superblocks so that each of the submounts has its own device ID.  To do
    so, we need to split all mount-specific information off of fuse_conn
    into a new fuse_mount structure, so that multiple mounts can share a
    single fuse_conn.

The vulnerable construct (skipping igrab when server does not implement open) remains present. The fix is not included.
